HARVARD UNIVERSITY 

OCT 14 1940 

OF GRADUATE SCHOOL PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION BARNSTABLE COUNTY Assessors Figures by Towns from 1865 to 1935 at Five Year Intervals 

Compiled under the direction of

George W. Westcott Extension Economist Data From Annual Reports of "Aggregates of Polls, Property, and Taxes" 

issued by the State of Massachusetts

Massachusetts State College, United States Department of Agriculture and County Extension Services in Agriculture and Home Economics Cooperating. 

C May, 1937

FOREWORD 

The tabulations in this circular are based entirely upon assessors' figures taken from the annual state reports entitled, "Aggregates of Polls, Property, and Taxes", issued by the Secretary of the Commonwealth from 1865 (Tabulations in this circular only go back to 1865) to 1907 inclusive; by the Tax Commissioner from 1908 to 1918; and by the Commissioner of Corporations and Taxation from 1919 to date. 

Assessments were made as of May 1 until 1911. From 1911 to 1934 inclusive, assessments were made as of April 1. From 1935 to acte, assessments have been made as of January 1. 

This circular represents an effort to bring eli assessors' figures, available from these reports, under one cover for five year intervals from 1865 to date, in order that they may be roudily available for local leaders and field workers engaged in developing county agricultural policies and programs. 

It is assumed that all who use this circular will appreciate the shortcomings of statistics and the necessity for using common sense when interpreting them. Obviously these tabulations are only as accurate as assessors' reports and all appreciate the nature and amount of tolerance and judgment necessary on the part of local assessing authorities. In spite of the inaccuracies which may exist in these figures, it is felt that they have value as another source of information to show past trends in taxable valuations, property taxes assessed, tax rates, numbers of dwelling houses, and livestock. 

All of the annual reports from which these figures were taken are available, and if annual figures are desired, (rather than those at five year intervals) they may be secured from the Department of Agricultural Economics, Massachusetts State College, Amherst, Mass.

May, 1937

FOREWORD 

The tabulations in this circular are based entirely upon assessors' figures taken from the annual state reports entitled, "Aggregates of Polis, Property, and Taxes", issued by the Secretary of the Commonwealth from 1865 (Tabulations in this circular only go back to 1865) to 1907 inclusive; by the Tax Commissioner from 1908 to 1918; and by the Commissioner of Corporations and Taxstion from 1919 to date. 

Assessments were made as of May 1 until 1911. From 1911 to 1934 inclusive, assessments were made as of April 1. From 1935 to ante, assessments have been made as of January 1. 

This circular represents an effort to bring eli assessors' figures, available from these reports, under one cover for five year intervals from 1865 to date, in order that they may be roudily available for local leaders and field workers engaged in developing county agricultural policies and prograins.

It is assumed that all who use this circular will appreciate the shortcomings of statistics and the necessity for using common sense when interpreting them. Obviously these tabulations are only as accurate as assessore' reports and all appreciate the nature and amount of tolerance and judgment necessary on the part of local assessing authorities. In spite of the inaccuracies which may exist in these figures, it is felt that they have value as another source of information to show past trends in tarable valuations, property taxes assessed, tax rates, numbers of dwelling houses, end livestock. 

All of the annual reports from which these figures were taken are available, and if annual figures are desired, (rather than those at five year intervals) they may be secured from the Department of Agricultural Economics, Massachusetts State College, Amherst, Mass.
